**Subject: Knocknacarra reading club – attendance update and Corrib Courier enquiry**

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to write before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November, because I have some very good news about the Tuesday club, and also something I should have handled better.

The club has been running since September 2025, from 3.30 to 4.45 in the upstairs meeting room at Knocknacarra library. When we started, attendance really was low: we had five children most weeks in September. By mid-October that had risen to nine, and last Tuesday, 3 November, we had fourteen children. It feels like a different club now.

It is not just the numbers, either. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. Another boy, who would not open a book in September, asked last week if he could take two home with him. That is the sort of progress an attendance sheet does not quite capture, and it has been a joy to see.

We have also had a wonderfully generous donation from Declan Moran, who owns Salthill Book Nook: 120 books, mostly suitable for the 6–9 age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. Having such a choice of books has given the sessions a real lift.

I understand why your email of 30 October proposed pausing the club from January. Attendance had been poor, and the hall insurance is going up. The insurance difficulty remains, and I do not want to make light of it, but the attendance position has changed considerably. Would you be willing to look at the new figures before the meeting on the 18th and reconsider the pause? It would be a terrible pity to stop now, just as the club has taken off.

The second matter is my own doing. I met Orla Keane, a reporter with the Corrib Courier, our local weekly, at the farmers’ market. I got carried away telling her how well the club was going and said, “come along any Tuesday”. She would now like to come on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I was wrong not to check with you first, plain and simple, and I am sorry. I know the policy perfectly well: there can be no photographs of children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms. I would much rather you heard this directly from me than from Orla or anyone else.

I can ring Orla straight away and put the visit on hold until you have decided. Nothing will go ahead without your approval. The coverage could be wonderful for the club and for Corrib Reading Partners, but only if it is done properly. If you are willing for the visit to proceed, I am happy to collect the consent forms myself, make sure everything is in order before the 24th, and follow whatever arrangements you want around the photography. If you would rather it did not happen, I will explain that to Orla.

Thank you for all the work you do coordinating the volunteers. I am thrilled with the way the children have settled in and begun to think of themselves as readers. I hope the new numbers will give us a good basis for a positive discussion about the club’s future on the 18th.

With best wishes,

[Your name]
